ai.title: Strengthen script and git command restrictions
ai.summary: System prompts updated to strictly forbid running scripts, git commits, or pushes without explicit user permission. `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt/agent-instructions.md` now mandate asking for confirmation before executing potentially destructive commands. This change aims to prevent costly accidents and production breakages caused by unauthorized agent actions.

eli5.text: The AI assistant is now stricter about not running dangerous commands on its own; it must ask you for permission before executing scripts, making git commits, or pushing changes to remote repositories. This affects anyone who interacts with the assistant, as it will now pause and wait for your explicit confirmation before taking potentially destructive actions that could break production systems. If you look closely, you would notice the assistant no longer proceeds with these risky operations without first checking with you.

ai.title: Trim verbosity from gemini thinking guidelines
ai.summary: Removed two specific instruction lines from the guidelines in `backend/src/thinking-stream.ts`. The deleted rules previously mandated showing code excerpts with comments for changes and writing full planning documents during thinking. This reduction aligns with the capability of Claude 4, allowing the model to rely on its inherent reasoning strength rather than verbose structural constraints. The change affects the internal prompt construction for the thinking stream.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal thinking instructions were trimmed down, two specific rules that forced it to lay out code snippets with comments and write out full planning documents have been removed. If you reviewed the thinking output, you would notice it is no longer padded with those extra structures, just the actual reasoning. This affects the behind-the-scenes prompt that shapes how the assistant organizes its thoughts, and it is live today.
